_comment: Copy this to scripts/bench/scenarios.json (git-ignored), fill it in for your
hardware, and delete the `_template` key. The scripts refuse a file that still
has it, and refuse placeholder names.
Nothing here is guessed from your machine: model names, sizes and the
contexts that do or do not fit are things only you know, and a harness
that assumed them would induce the wrong condition and report a pass.
Sizes are the resident footprint in GB, which is weights plus KV cache at
the context you run them at, not the file size /api/tags reports. Read
them off `ollama ps` while the model is loaded.
Set host.platform to the output of `node -p process.platform` on the machine
that will run the scripts, so a copy of this file cannot be run on a different
one by mistake.
Run the harness against a runtime you control. The scripts load and unload models.

host.label: FILL-ME-IN: machine, accelerator, memory
host.notes: How the agent should see this host's accelerator budget, and anything unusual about it.

_comment: resident_gb above is measured at `fits`. The footprint is weights plus KV
cache and the second grows fast, so a pair that fits at a small context stops
fitting at a large one. That is what makes eviction inducible on a machine
with room for both models. Measure each of these on your host; the M4's
values are in scenarios.m4.json and are not a guide to yours.
For the reference controller. Workflow A holds `held` continuously.
Workflow B's step may run on any model in `acceptable`, in preference
order — the operator declares that, not Wicklee. `defer_allowed` lets
the wicklee policy wait rather than displace.
